newsitem.title: USA: NASA restores communications link with Mars rover.
newsitem.headline: NASA restores communications link with Mars rover.

text.p: Communications were restored on Saturday between the Pathfinder space craft and the Mars rover that will analyze the rocks and soil of the Red Planet.

The announcement by rover coordinator Matt Wallace brought cheers of relief from mission control staff here after more than 12 hours of nail-biting efforts to make contact with the rover Sojourner on the planet's surface and salvage the scientific aspects of the $266-million project.
"This is just fantastic news. I feel like we have been invited back to the party," Wallace said, in explaining that signals had been received from rover via the Pathfiner lander.
Earlier in the day, officials of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration said that communications between Sojourner and the lander were virtually dead as a result of a software problem.
But after recycling the modem, the six-wheeled rover was now able to communicate with the lander and in turn with Earth, Wallace said.
The rover was next scheduled to follow instructions and roll down the ramp onto the surface of Mars later on Saturday.
